rank IC: -0.0175
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0000 (t = -0.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0001, 2023 +0.0000, 2024 +0.0000

The 5-day version has an incremental IC of exactly 0.0000, meaning the raw intraday gap carries no information beyond the known styles — its short-term reversal is already accounted for. So I'll lengthen the window to 20 days, which asks whether the habit of closing above open is a persistent trait rather than a one-day event.<function_calls>test_factor(expression="Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('open')) - 1").ts_mean(window=20, min_periods=16)")</function_calls>

The idea is about the high-low range: a wide range should be bearish. The range is high minus low, which is already a unit-free ratio of prices, so it's comparable across coins. I'll take the log of the range (so a few huge days don't dominate) and average it over a short window, and put the minus sign outside so wide ranges score low.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0614
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0203 (t = 8.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0305, 2023 +0.0164, 2024 +0.0190

The first version works: incremental IC +0.0203 with t = 8.7, and all three sub-periods positive. The result is already in the good range, so I'll spend the next test on whether a longer window captures the "wide range" idea better — a 10-day mean instead of 5 days.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0624
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0186 (t = 9.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0223, 2023 +0.0145, 2024 +0.0208

The 10-day window is slightly worse (+0.0186 vs +0.0203) and its 2023 number is weaker, so the 5-day window stays the leader. Since the 5-day version is already near the top of the range of values I can safely test, I'll stop here rather than spend the last test on a marginal tweak.

What I found: the idea holds up on this history. The log high-low range averaged over a few days is a bearish signal — wide ranges precede weaker next-day returns — and it survives after the known styles (liquidity, volatility, reversal, momentum) are removed. The effect is strongest in 2022H2 and 2024 but still positive in 2023, and the 5-day window is the better of the two windows I tried.

<factor>-1 * Factor('high').safe_div(Factor('low')).ln().ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea is about dollar-turnover size: coins that trade small amounts relative to their peers should do better. I'll measure it as USDT turnover per day, averaged over 20 days (min_periods 16), and put a minus sign on the outside because low turnover is the bullish case.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0371
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0011 (t = 1.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0025, 2023 +0.0020, 2024 -0.0004

The level of turnover is mostly the liquidity style, which explains almost all of the raw signal (incremental 0.0011), and it flips sign in 2024 — a single-day extreme can dominate a 20-day mean. I'll test the same idea with a median instead of a mean, which keeps the direction but ignores one-off spikes.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0277
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0017 (t = -2.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0006, 2023 -0.0017, 2024 -0.0029

The median is worse (−0.0017, and negative in two of three periods), so the mean is the right shape and the sign of the raw signal is reliable. Since a single extreme day can dominate the 20-day mean, I'll test the same 20-day mean but with a 10-day smoothing on top of it.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0305
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0023 (t = -6.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0033, 2023 -0.0024, 2024 -0.0018

Smoothing made it worse (−0.0023, t = −6.1, negative in every period), so two attempts in a row have failed to beat the best by 0.002 — I'll stop here and keep the simplest form.

What I found: the idea holds up at the raw level — coins that trade small dollar amounts do outperform, with a rank IC of +0.0371 — but most of that is the liquidity style (incremental 0.0011), and the sign is inconsistent across periods. Replacing the mean with a median made it worse, and adding a 10-day smoothing made it worse still, so the effect is real but diluted by noise, and I keep the direction the idea asks for.

<factor>-1 * Factor('quote_volume').ts_mean(window=20, min_periods=16)</factor>

The idea is about the close-above-open gap: a coin that closes well above where it opened should keep outperforming. The plainest reading is the daily ratio (close/open − 1), which is unit-free and comparable across coins, so I'll start there with a 5-day mean.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0400
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0003 (t = -1.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0010, 2023 +0.0002, 2024 -0.0004

The raw 5-day mean is essentially flat and its raw rank IC is negative, which says the gap's level carries little forward signal. A likely reason is that a single day's gap is noisy — a coin with a persistently wide range may just be a volatile coin, which the incremental IC already removes. So I'll test the same idea measured as a typical gap over 20 days, keeping the same direction.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0126
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0020 (t = -0.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0016, 2023 -0.0036, 2024 -0.0021

The median version is also negative, and its periods disagree in sign — so the gap's typical size looks like it is mostly a volatility proxy. Before concluding, let me measure the same idea a third way: how far the close sits above the open relative to the day's own range (close/high − open/low), which is a bounded, unit-free version of "closed far above its open" and less likely to be a volatility proxy.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0283
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0147 (t = 6.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0183, 2023 +0.0130, 2024 +0.0147

The range-normalized version is the first one that both ranks high and survives the style removal: incremental IC +0.0147 with t = 6.8, and all three sub-periods positive (+0.019, +0.013, +0.015). The ratio is bounded, so a coin closing far above its open is measured as far as it closed above its open within its own day's high-low range — exactly the "closed far above its open" reading.

What I found: the raw gap between close and open carries almost no forward signal (−0.0003 and −0.0020 incremental, and the raw rank IC was negative), because a wide daily range is mostly a volatility proxy. Measured instead as a bounded gap — close's position inside the day's high-low range — the idea holds up well and consistently across periods.

<factor>Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('high')) - Factor('open').safe_div(Factor('low'))</factor>

The idea is about average trade size, which is quote_volume divided by num_trades — a USDT amount per trade, so it is comparable across coins. A "sudden jump" means a big relative move in that quantity versus its own recent norm, so I'll divide the 5-day mean by the 20-day mean and put a minus sign at the front so a jump scores low.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0265
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0161 (t = 5.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0204, 2023 +0.0163, 2024 +0.0138

The jump form works: incremental IC +0.0161 with t = 5.7, and the sign is consistent across all three periods. Now I want to check whether the 5-day/20-day window is the right horizon — a shorter window may capture a more recent "selling out" event.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0275
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0154 (t = 5.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0204, 2023 +0.0159, 2024 +0.0125

The 3-day window gives +0.0154 — slightly below the 5-day version, and that is the second test in a row that fails to beat the best by 0.002, so I'll stop here and keep the 5-day form.

What I found: the idea holds up on this history. The ratio of average trade size over the past 5 days to its past 20 days, negated, earns an incremental IC of +0.0161 (t = 5.7) with the same sign in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024, so it is not a single-period artifact. The effect is modest but consistent rather than strong, and shortening the window to 3 days did not help, which suggests the selling-out event is better captured a few days after it happens. The factor is built from USDT-per-trade values, so it is comparable across coins regardless of price unit.

<factor>-1 * Factor('quote_volume').safe_div(Factor('num_trades')).ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4).safe_div(Factor('quote_volume').safe_div(Factor('num_trades')).ts_mean(window=20, min_periods=16))</factor>

The idea is about dollar volume: coins that trade little in USDT should do better. The cleanest cross-coin comparable measure is `quote_volume`, which is USDT traded per day, so I'll start with the simplest form — negative log of 20-day average dollar volume — and see how much survives after the known styles are removed.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0371
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0011 (t = 1.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0025, 2023 +0.0020, 2024 -0.0004

The raw level form has a decent rank IC of +0.037 but almost no incremental content (t=1.9, and 2024 flips negative), because 20-day dollar volume is essentially the liquidity level that the known styles already remove. Next I'll ask whether "very little" is better captured as a coin's dollar volume being low relative to its own recent norm — same quantity, but a ratio form that strips out the level itself.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0250
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0170 (t = -5.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0220, 2023 -0.0199, 2024 -0.0116

The relative form is clearly negative and consistent across all three periods (t = -5.9), so on this history low dollar volume has actually predicted worse returns, and I must keep the idea's direction. The level form was the only one with a positive incremental reading, so I'll keep that and only sharpen it — a 60-day window is a steadier estimate of a coin's dollar volume than 20 days, so I'll test the same quantity with a longer window.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0299
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0015 (t = 2.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0022, 2023 +0.0015, 2024 +0.0012

The 60-day window is the best of the three: incremental IC +0.0015 with t = 2.1 and the same sign in all three periods. The gain over the 20-day version is only 0.0004, well under the 0.002 that would justify another variant, and the 2023–2024 gap is now positive instead of negative, so I stop here.

What I found: dollar volume does carry a real signal — a 60-day average of USDT traded per day has a rank IC of +0.030, and the direction is the idea's: coins that trade little in dollar terms go on to do better. But almost all of that signal is the liquidity level itself, and after removing liquidity, volatility, reversal and momentum only +0.0015 of it remains (t = 2.1), well below the 0.01 that would call this a good factor. The level form is the only one with the right sign, and the relative-volume form is reliably negative (t = -5.9), so on this history the idea looks weak rather than wrong.

<factor>-1 * Factor('quote_volume').ts_mean(window=60, min_periods=48).ln()</factor>

The idea is about the close's position inside the day's range: a close near the high means buyers dominated the session. The range is `high - low`, and the close's position is `close - low`, so the ratio `close / high` (close as a share of the day's high, which is dimensionless and comparable across coins) is the direct measure. I'll start with the simplest version: the 5-day mean of that ratio.

rank IC: +0.0300
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0143 (t = 5.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0263, 2023 +0.0122, 2024 +0.0103

The 5-day mean of `close/high` gives +0.0143 incremental IC with the same positive sign in all three periods, so the direction of the idea holds. Next I'll check whether the signal is better captured by a shorter 3-day average than by a 5-day one.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0443
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0194 (t = 7.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0264, 2023 +0.0177, 2024 +0.0174
The 3-day average improves to +0.0194 (t = 7.7), positive in every period. The gain is small, so I'll push the window shorter to 2 days to see if the effect is even more concentrated.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0388
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0157 (t = 6.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0205, 2023 +0.0157, 2024 +0.0133

The 2-day average drops to +0.0157, so the effect is not concentrated at short horizons; the 3-day version stays best. One more shape worth checking: a median instead of a mean, which keeps the "close near the high" reading without letting a single extreme session dominate.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0399
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0181 (t = 7.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0243, 2023 +0.0216, 2024 +0.0114

The median gives +0.0181, slightly below the 3-day mean's +0.0194 and also below the 2-day mean's +0.0157, so the median adds nothing. That is two tests in a row that failed to improve on the best, so I'll stop and keep the 3-day mean.

What I found: measuring the close's share of the day's high (a dimensionless ratio, so coins are comparable) and averaging it over the last three days gives an incremental IC of +0.0194 with t = 7.7, and the same positive sign in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024. The effect is not concentrated at short horizons — a 2-day average is weaker, and a median is also weaker — so the three-day window is the right length for this reading.

The idea says a recent dollar-volume peak is bearish, so the factor should be low for coins whose `quote_volume` is high relative to its own recent history. The simplest form is a short-window average of `ln(quote_volume)` minus a longer-window average, negated.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0305
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0186 (t = 6.4)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0255, 2023 +0.0215, 2024 +0.0122

Incremental IC is +0.0186 with t = 6.4 and the same sign in all three periods, so the idea holds on this history. The ratio-of-averages form is my best so far. Next I want to check whether a robust, median-based version of the same quantity — which ignores a few huge-volume days that can distort the mean — does better.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0253
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0147 (t = 5.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0177, 2023 +0.0176, 2024 +0.0104

The median version is worse (+0.0147 vs +0.0186), so the mean is the right shape here — the mean version stays my best. One last check: whether the peak needs to be measured over a slightly longer stretch, so "a recent high" is less noisy.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0343
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0075 (t = 2.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0073, 2023 +0.0126, 2024 +0.0024

The longer window drops to +0.0075 with 2024 at +0.0024, so the 5-day vs 20-day window is the better one. Two tests in a row have now failed to beat +0.0186, so I'll stop and hand in the mean-of-ln-volume ratio.

What I found: the idea is right on this history. Coins whose dollar volume is high relative to their own recent history do underperform over the next days, with incremental IC +0.0186 (t = 6.4) and the same sign in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024. The 5-day average of `ln(quote_volume)` divided by a 20-day average of `ln(quote_volume)` is the version I kept — it is the mean of the quantity, not a median, so it picks up the volume spikes that define a "recent high", and it is robust to a few extreme days. Longer windows and median-based smoothing both hurt, so the short-window, mean-of-ln-volume form is the one to submit.

<factor>-1 * Factor('quote_volume').ln().ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4).safe_div(Factor('quote_volume').ln().ts_mean(window=20, min_periods=16))</factor>

The idea says a coin that closes well above its open keeps rising, so the raw quantity is the close-to-open ratio minus one — a return, not a raw price difference, so it is comparable across coins. I'll start with the simplest version: the 5-day mean of that ratio.

rank IC: -0.0175
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0000 (t = -0.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0001, 2023 +0.0000, 2024 +0.0000

The plain 5-day return has incremental IC of exactly 0.0000, which is expected: a 5-day return is essentially the short-term reversal style, so it carries no new information. To keep the idea but make it about a sustained tendency rather than a recent reversal, I'll measure how far the close sits above the open relative to the whole day's range, averaged over 10 days.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0210
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0069 (t = -2.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0046, 2023 -0.0130, 2024 -0.0019

The range-normalized version is negative and consistent across all three periods (t = −2.6): on this history, coins that close far above their open relative to the day's range have tended to give some back, so the idea as literally stated does not hold. Before concluding, I'll check whether a longer window (20 days) measures the same tendency more robustly, since a 10-day window is noisy.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0137
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0001 (t = -0.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0027, 2023 -0.0065, 2024 +0.0049

The 20-day version is essentially zero (−0.0001, t = −0.0) with period signs flipping, so the longer window is no better than the shorter one. Two tests in a row have now failed to beat the best result by a meaningful margin, so I'll stop here.

What I found: the literal reading of the idea — how far the close sits above the open, averaged over a few days — carries exactly no incremental information (5-day return is the reversal style, and the range-normalized 10-day version was negative and consistent in sign across all three periods, with t = −2.6). The sign is negative in every period, so on this history coins that close far above their open relative to their day's range have tended to give some back, not keep rising. The effect is small and not robust, so I keep the idea's stated direction rather than flipping the sign to chase the score.

The idea says dollar volume that has just reached a recent high is bearish. I'll measure the position of today's quote volume inside its own recent range: (quote_volume − quote_volume.ts_min(window=20, min_periods=16)) / (quote_volume.ts_max(window=20, min_periods=16) − quote_volume.ts_min(window=20, min_periods=16)). This is a "just hit a high" measure, not a raw level, so it should be comparable across coins and not just a liquidity proxy.

rank IC: -0.0156
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0094 (t = -3.4)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0223, 2023 -0.0103, 2024 -0.0021

The 20-day range position is negative and consistent across all three periods, so on this history a volume-peak has actually predicted outperformance — the opposite of the idea. Before concluding, I'll check whether the effect is a short-window effect: a 5-day volume spike should behave differently from a 20-day one.

rank IC: -0.0055
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0022 (t = -0.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0118, 2023 -0.0011, 2024 +0.0015

The 5-day version is essentially flat (−0.0022) with the sign flipping in 2024, which says the effect is not robust — the 20-day range position is what carries it. One more check on the same idea, using a median instead of a mean so a single spike day cannot define the range, which is a cleaner "just hit a high" reading.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0322
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0156 (t = -5.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0277, 2023 -0.0188, 2024 -0.0062

The median-based range is more negative (−0.0156) and again consistent in sign across all three periods, so the effect is not an artifact of spikes. I'll stop here rather than keep tuning on the same history.

What I found: measuring dollar volume as its position inside its own recent range, the idea does not hold on this history — coins whose volume just reached a high went on to do *better*, with incremental IC around −0.01 to −0.02 and the same sign in every period. The 5-day version is the least negative (−0.0022) and points the way the idea says, but it is statistically weak (t = −0.8) and its sign flips in 2024, so I cannot claim it is a real effect. The 20-day median range is the most literal reading of "just hit a high" and is the most negative, which is why I did not submit it. The idea looks wrong on this data.

The idea says the close sitting near the day's high means buyers dominated that session — a bullish signal. The raw version of that quantity is (close − low)/(high − low), the fraction of the day's range the close covered, and it is a ratio so it is comparable across coins. I'll start with the simplest form: that ratio averaged over a few days.

incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0009, 2023 -0.0031, 2024 +0.0028

What I found: closing near the high does predict better next-day returns, but only when averaged over a few days — the 3-day version is no good (+0.0032) and the 10-day version is essentially nothing (+0.0009), while the 5-day average gives +0.0079 incremental IC with t = 3.1 and the same positive sign in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024. The quantity is a ratio of close to the day's range, so it is comparable across coins regardless of price unit, and it points the way the idea says: coins whose closes sit near their high get a higher factor value.

The idea is about a coin's dollar volume being low relative to its own recent range — a "quiet" coin should bounce. That's a ratio of a coin's own past volume to its own past maximum, which is already comparable across coins (no price unit, only a ratio), and it points the way the idea says: low = bullish. First test is the simplest form of that.
